title: Mixed timestamp conventions inside the 2025 increment
evidence: 2107_irradiance_15m_data_2025.csv uses utc_measured_on; 2107_meter_15m_data_2025.csv uses local measured_on. Overlap test vs 2024 files: meter identical at 0 h shift (share 1.0); POA identical at -7 h (0.878) and -8 h (0.113). results/phase1/file_overlap_check.json PHASE 2: Increments ingested with lineage as EXCLUDED_BY_SCOPE; 2024 vs 2025 overlaps are 29,175 meter + 66,103 POA rows, all identical within 1e-6 after per-file conversion (0 conflicts).
affected_data_or_calculation: Pairing AC and POA from the 2024-2025 increments
proposed_treatment: Exclude 2024-2025 increments from the v1 primary window. If later used as an extra holdout, convert each file with its own convention and re-verify

title: Local clock with daylight saving time
evidence: measured_on is local PST8PDT. Spring-forward 02:00-02:59 rows absent every year (28 meter / 72 POA nonexistent slots 2017-2023); fall-back 01:xx hour present once, no duplicates. Summer weighted midpoints ~+55-60 min vs winter. results/phase1/dst_transition_check.csv, noon_timing_2017_2023.csv PHASE 2: 86 in-scope TIME_AMBIGUOUS rows (24 meter, 62 POA); 172 DST_AMBIGUOUS expected intervals (48 meter, 124 POA); 0 nonexistent rows; check V08 PASS. PHASE 3: the daylight window (sun > 5 deg) excludes all night intervals; 0 DST-ambiguous intervals fall inside the window in the development period (check P08).
affected_data_or_calculation: Timestamp conversion; daily aggregation; 23/25-hour days
proposed_treatment: docs/timestamp_policy.md: UTC timeline; spring hour not counted missing; every ambiguous fall-back row TIME_AMBIGUOUS with both UTC candidates (never resolved from occurrence count or file order); their intervals DST_AMBIGUOUS. Whether these night-time rows affect PR depends on Phase 3's reporting window and treatment of night-time intervals and energy

title: Interval alignment and absolute timing not fully verified
evidence: 'L' (interval start) alignment is a metadata claim only. Relative alignment: meter vs 24-inverter sum best at 0 shift (corr 0.991, 2024); POA vs inverter sum best at 0 shift at 5-min resolution in 2024 Nov-Feb (0.969 vs 0.907 at -5 min) and inside the primary window in 2018-11 to 2019-02 (0.880 vs 0.843) and 2021-11 to 2022-02 (0.977 vs 0.959). Meter vs inverter lag tested in 2024 only. Main-file 15-min bucket test peaks weakly at -5 min (0.960 vs 0.955). POA weighted daily midpoint about 0-21 min later than calculated solar noon in standard-time months (method confounded by weather asymmetry); meter midpoint ~13-18 min earlier than POA midpoint (confounded by clipping and heat losses). results/phase1/supplementary_checks.json, boundary_check_2024.json, boundary_check_2017_2023.json PHASE 2: Observed discrepancy under tested model assumptions (pvlib Ineichen clear sky, isotropic transposition, 25 deg tilt, metadata azimuth 180 deg; clear days by shape corr >= 0.998 and energy ratio 0.85-1.15): on 520 clear days 2018-2023 measured POA aligns best with the model shifted ~-11 min (median; IQR -12..-11), stable across years and seasons. With an assumed azimuth of 190 deg the medians are 0 (May-Aug) and -2 (Nov-Feb); 200 deg overshoots (+12 / +7). Orientation (array or POA sensor), timestamp convention, clock offset and model limitations all remain possible explanations; the analysis proves none of them. results/phase2/interval_label_check.csv, azimuth_sensitivity_check.csv
affected_data_or_calculation: Interval pairing; timing-consistency check (Phase 5); minimum detectable timestamp-shift severity (Phase 6)
current_status: unresolved: stable observed discrepancy measured; cause unknown
proposed_treatment: Keep interval-start labels as the documented assumption; timestamps and metadata azimuth unchanged. Phase 5 timing checks compare against the site's own baseline discrepancy measured on development data under a stated model, not against zero; Phase 6 shift severities stated relative to that baseline. Geometry-based daylight rules (incl. the 10 deg A-DAYZERO criterion) carry edge uncertainty of similar size. PHASE 4: timing check uses clear-sky reference with development baseline -11 min and 8 min threshold; discrepancy not corrected

title: POA daytime missing data and multi-day gaps
evidence: Main POA file (2017-11 to 2023-11): 5.7% of 08:00-17:00 5-min slots missing overall, but very uneven by year: 2017 85.9%, 2018 10.4%, 2019 0.3%, 2020 0.04%, 2021 1.3%, 2022 8.1%, 2023 0.1% (see I17 for the near-empty start); 138 days with >1 h daytime gap; 7 gaps >1 day, largest 2022-02-18 13:20 to 2022-03-07 11:25 (16.9 days), 2018-01-08 to 2018-01-22 (14.0 days). For 2018-2023 daytime missingness is flat across hours 08-16 (~3.4%), consistent with dropouts, not report-by-exception logging. results/phase1/gap_recount.json, poa_daytime_coverage.json, supplementary_checks.json PHASE 2: 100,215 POA expected intervals generated as EXPECTED_ROW_MISSING (no fill); 36,910 IRREGULAR_INTERVAL flags.
affected_data_or_calculation: PR denominator coverage; INSUFFICIENT_DATA rate; choice of fault-injection windows
current_status: confirmed; kept as missing in Phase 2
proposed_treatment: Build expected grid; keep missing distinct from zero; days below coverage threshold become INSUFFICIENT_DATA. Inject missing-data faults only into windows without pre-existing gaps and record pre-existing gaps per case

title: Meter missing rows
evidence: After removing spring-forward artefacts: 292 genuine missing 15-min rows in 2017-2023 (108 between 08:00-17:00; 3 days with >1 h daytime gap), mainly 2021-07-16/17 and 2023-05-12. Zero genuine missing rows in the 2024 and 2025 meter files. results/phase1/gap_recount.json PHASE 2: 292 generated EXPECTED_ROW_MISSING meter rows, identical to Phase 1 recount.
affected_data_or_calculation: Daily AC energy coverage
proposed_treatment: Kept as EXPECTED_ROW_MISSING (no fill)

title: Daylight meter zeros while POA is high
evidence: 43 runs / 343 15-min intervals with meter <= 0 kW and POA > 200 W/m2 (2017-2024 local-clock files); 42 runs not followed by a catch-up value. Cause unknown (outage, curtailment, or communication). results/phase1/daylight_zero_events.csv PHASE 2: Kept OBSERVED_ZERO with DAYLIGHT_ZERO_UNRESOLVED flag (rule A-DAYZERO: solar elevation > 10 deg, or any POA > 200 W/m2 in the same meter interval): 2,988 meter intervals on 564 local days, 27 days with >= 30 flagged intervals; concentrated in 2022-02/03, 2018-04 and 2022-06, which coincide with long POA gaps (possible site-wide data or plant outages, unconfirmed). All 41 in-scope Phase 1 runs covered; 2 runs in the 2024 increment are EXCLUDED_BY_SCOPE with value_state OBSERVED_ZERO (check V14). PHASE 3 (development period 2018-02..2020-01): 886 window meter intervals on 189 days read exactly 0, mostly 06-07 h and 18-19 h local, with POA mostly 25-200 W/m2 where comparable non-zero intervals produce a median 27-52 kW; they carry 1-5% of paired irradiation on most review days. They remain paired as observed zeros and withhold the day (UNRESOLVED_ZERO_OUTPUT).
affected_data_or_calculation: Observed zero vs missing distinction; PR on affected days; false alarms in Phase 7
proposed_treatment: Keep as observed zero in Phase 2 but flag; do not call these days clean. Review during Phase 7 alert adjudication

title: Catch-up spike after daylight zeros
evidence: 2018-02-18: 12:00 and 12:15 = 0 kW, 12:30 = 1783.68 kW (2.0x DC capacity), 12:45 = 679.04 kW, while POA steady ~985 W/m2. Only such event found with next value > 720 kW. results/phase1/daylight_zero_summary.json PHASE 2: meter_main:39695 raw 1783.68 at 2018-02-18 12:30 local (check V12).
affected_data_or_calculation: Interval AC power validity; daily energy for that day
proposed_treatment: INVALID_PHYSICAL under rule R-LIMITS (AC above the 893 kW conservative project screening bound, set at DC nameplate; not a universal physical ceiling) plus SUSPECTED_LOGGER_ARTEFACT A-CATCHUP on the spike and its 2 preceding zeros; raw value and source row retained

title: POA values capped at exactly 1400 W/m2
evidence: 11 rows exactly 1400.0 W/m2 (main file), all 12:00-14:59 in March; 51 rows > 1300 W/m2; same 1400.0 maximum in all three POA files. results/phase1/supplementary_checks.json PHASE 2: 13 rows exactly 1400 W/m2 (11 in scope) retained and flagged (check V13).
affected_data_or_calculation: POA range check; irradiation on a few cloud-enhancement intervals
proposed_treatment: Retained as OBSERVED_VALID with SUSPECTED_LOGGER_ARTEFACT A-CEILING flag

title: Conflicting date metadata and pre-commissioning output
evidence: JSON first/last_timestamp 2018-12-15 / 2023-11-15; index 2017-01-01 / 2024-11-30; files: meter from 2017-01-01 (first > 1 kW on 2017-01-16), POA from 2017-11-01; modules start_on 2017-11-01; night-time 0.1216 kW flat run 2017-01-18
affected_data_or_calculation: Usable analysis window
proposed_treatment: Meter rows before 2017-11-01 are EXCLUDED_BY_SCOPE (outside v1 window)

title: Coverage gap and overlapping increments
evidence: Main files end 2023-11-01 23:55 (POA) and 2023-11-09 23:30 (meter); 2024 files start 2024-01-01 (Nov-Dec 2023 absent). 2024 POA file ends 2024-11-01 although the change log says single-year files cover Jan-Dec; 2025 files start 2024-02-01 and overlap the 2024 files
affected_data_or_calculation: Window selection; avoiding double counting
proposed_treatment: Primary window uses main files only; Phase 4 chooses split inside that window

title: Inverter nameplate assumption contradicted by data
evidence: Assumed 24 x 27.6 kW = 662.4 kW from model name; 4509 meter values exceed it. Inverter data (2024): per-inverter max 30.08-30.10 kW; inverter sum max 721.4 kW; meter ceiling 705-708 kW = ~0.98 x sum. results/phase1/boundary_check_2024.json
affected_data_or_calculation: Clipping interpretation
proposed_treatment: Not a data fault. Plant output clips at ~707 kW at the meter (inverter limit). Phase 5 must distinguish power clipping from POA flatline

title: POA sensor type and plane undocumented; no redundant irradiance sensor
evidence: Weather station manufacturer 'Unknown', no model; POA plane inferred from field name 'poa_irradiance'; only one irradiance channel in metadata (125 metrics)
affected_data_or_calculation: POA calibration; any claim about irradiance accuracy
proposed_treatment: State as limitation. Without a second sensor, irradiance calibration and drift cannot be verified; drift is out of scope for v1

title: Meter value quantisation
evidence: Most common non-zero meter values are 0.64, 1.28, 1.92, 2.56 kW (0.64 kW steps). results/phase1/file_profiles.json
affected_data_or_calculation: Low-power intervals; stale-value checks on power
proposed_treatment: Note resolution in data card. Inference only: values may be derived from energy pulses

title: Flat plant power at high irradiance
evidence: 2022-04-05 11:45-13:30: 8 consecutive meter values 646.4 kW while POA varied 833-1057 W/m2 (the only daytime non-zero meter run >= 2 h in 2017-2023). results/phase1/file_profiles.json
affected_data_or_calculation: Flatline detection (power side); review burden
proposed_treatment: Probable clipping/limit (below the usual ~707 kW ceiling, so not proven). Flatline fault in v1 targets POA only; record as context

title: Sparse night-time POA records
evidence: ~27% of 5-min POA slots missing at 00:00-05:00 vs ~3.4% at 08:00-16:00. results/phase1/supplementary_checks.json
affected_data_or_calculation: Overall completeness metric (basic check)
proposed_treatment: Night sparsity appears as MISSING expected intervals; Phase 3 must judge completeness on daylight only

title: No negative meter values
evidence: Meter minimum 0.0 kW in all files; 0 negative rows
affected_data_or_calculation: Night-time consumption
proposed_treatment: Night consumption is probably not recorded or is floored at zero (assumption). No effect on PR numerator over daylight

title: POA nearly empty at the start of the record
evidence: Daytime (08:00-17:00) POA slots missing: 2017-11 89.6%, 2017-12 82.3%, 2018-01 69.1%, then 2018-03 12.9% and 2018-04 40.3%; 2018-05 onward near complete. Only 2,575 POA rows in all of 2017. results/phase1/poa_daytime_coverage.json
affected_data_or_calculation: Usable paired coverage; start of the primary window
proposed_treatment: Treat usable paired coverage as starting 2018-02; Mar-Apr 2018 partially covered. Phase 4 chooses the split with this in view

title: Meter and inverter sum agree less closely in some years
evidence: Meter vs 24-inverter sum (15-min, meter > 100 kW): median ratio stable 0.976-0.985 every year, but correlation varies: 2019 0.978, 2023 0.974, 2020 0.957, 2022 0.896, 2021 0.798, 2018 0.763. results/phase1/boundary_check_2017_2023.json
affected_data_or_calculation: Confidence in AC data on affected periods; Phase 7 alert adjudication
proposed_treatment: Not needed for PR (meter is the AC source), but low agreement marks periods where either the meter or inverter data has problems. Locate the disagreeing periods in Phase 2 profiling and keep them out of fault-injection windows unless explained

title: Incomplete POA groups inside 15-min meter intervals
evidence: Daylight meter intervals (solar elevation > 10 deg) by usable 5-min POA intervals: 3 of 3 = 84,853; 2 = 252; 1 = 70; 0 = 4,280. Every meter interval contains exactly 3 expected POA intervals (check V18). results/phase2/poa_15min_group_completeness.csv
affected_data_or_calculation: Pairing AC energy with POA irradiation in Phase 3; INSUFFICIENT_DATA rate
proposed_treatment: Phase 3: incomplete POA groups exclude the whole meter interval from E_AC and H_POA (POA_MISSING); 846 window intervals (211.5 h) excluded in the development period; days below coverage thresholds are INSUFFICIENT_DATA

title: Daylight meter zeros coincide with long POA gaps
evidence: Months with most DAYLIGHT_ZERO_UNRESOLVED meter flags (2022-02: 381, 2022-03: 251, 2018-04: 135, 2022-06: 129) overlap the POA gaps of 2022-02-18 to 03-07, 2018-04-13 to 04-23 and 2022-06-08 to 06-17
affected_data_or_calculation: Choice of fault-injection windows; alert burden on unmodified data
proposed_treatment: Treat as pre-existing site/data events; Phase 4 should avoid placing synthetic faults inside them and report them as unconfirmed alerts if detectors fire

title: High review burden from unresolved dawn/dusk zero output
evidence: Development period: 180 of 730 days (24.7%) REVIEW_REQUIRED, almost all for UNRESOLVED_ZERO_OUTPUT; zeros cluster at 06-07 h and 18-19 h local (results/phase3/daily_pr_dev.csv, paired_intervals_dev.parquet) PHASE 4: under experiment-v1 basic, development review days fall from 180 to 123 (MATERIAL_ZERO_OUTPUT 121, SUSPICIOUS_ZERO_OUTPUT 15, SUSPICIOUS_POA_ZERO 2); results/phase4/development_policy_comparison.csv
affected_data_or_calculation: Share of reportable days; alert burden in Phase 7
proposed_treatment: Phase 4 decides the final withholding policy for unresolved zeros (e.g. materiality by irradiation share) before evaluation; any change is recorded as a development decision, not tuned on evaluation data

title: Daily PR varies for reasons other than data faults
evidence: Passed development days: reported PR median 0.793, IQR 0.752-0.828, range 0.552-0.952; median PR 0.87 at H <= 1 kWh/m2 vs 0.785 at H 5-9. 33 passed days with H >= 3 kWh/m2 read PR > 0.85 (max 0.90 at H up to 7.3), mostly Oct-Jan and Mar. Possible contributors (untested): no temperature correction, inverter clipping near 707 kW on 893 kW DC, irradiance-dependent effects, POA sensor under-reading/calibration
affected_data_or_calculation: Interpreting PR changes from injected faults (Phases 6-7)
proposed_treatment: Compare faulted vs unmodified PR for the same day and window; never treat a PR level alone as evidence of a fault or of normal operation

title: Reporting window (5 deg) and daylight-zero flag (10 deg or POA > 200) thresholds do not align
evidence: Development period: 542 paired window zeros on 226 days carry no DAYLIGHT_ZERO_UNRESOLVED flag and withhold nothing; 50 of those days are CHECKS_PASSED, where the zeros carry a median 0.3% of paired H and change PR by at most 1.29 pp (diagnostic comparison). results/phase3/unflagged_zero_days_dev.csv
affected_data_or_calculation: Which days withhold for unresolved zero output; small low bias in some passed-day PR
current_status: resolved by experiment-v1 (policy covers whole window from 5 deg)
proposed_treatment: experiment-v1 zero policy replaces the Phase 2 flag as the withholding rule; flag kept as context. Remaining zeros on basic-passed development days carry <= 0.98% of H (median -0.29 pp, max 0.68 pp PR effect)

title: Timing check inconclusive on most days, especially winter
evidence: Development: conclusive (clear-day) on 155 of 721 days; Dec 0, Jan 1, Feb 3 conclusive days (results/phase4/dev_timing_lags.csv). Meter-vs-POA reference rejected: 46% development alert burden PHASE 5 (tested implementation, development): 575 inconclusive (538 not clear, 20 best lag at +-90 boundary, 17 too few readings), 155 conclusive; 463 improved-passed days carry 'timing not verified'. PHASE 6 smoke (development, 3 shift windows passed unmodified): improved shift cases 10 DETECTED_SPECIFIC on the one conclusive day, 16 INCONCLUSIVE and 4 WITHHELD_OTHER on non-clear days. PHASE 7 (run1, evaluation): improved POA-shift cases 29/168 recognised, 113 inconclusive; timing applicability DJF 2%, MAM 13%, JJA 7%, SON 42%.
affected_data_or_calculation: Detection of timestamp shifts (Phase 7); many INCONCLUSIVE cases expected
current_status: confirmed in evaluation; accepted limitation of experiment-v3
proposed_treatment: Score INCONCLUSIVE separately; do not count as misses or detections; report by season

title: Phase 4 prototype timing gate deviated from the specified eligible-reading definition
evidence: Prototype used each 5-min POA reading's own solar elevation (> 5 deg at +2 min); specification (pinned in experiment-v2 A3) uses in-window meter-interval membership. Eligible counts differ by 1-3 edge readings on 161 development days; best lag differs on 39 days, all inconclusive; no status, reason or conclusiveness change (results/phase5/prototype_comparison.csv)
affected_data_or_calculation: Timing evidence values on inconclusive days only
current_status: resolved: implementation follows specification; prototype preserved as-is
proposed_treatment: None needed; documented in decision log D31

title: Clear-day timing gate is conservative and near-threshold on some days
evidence: run1: 7 of 8 summer shift-window counterparts failed the corr >= 0.998 / energy-ratio gate (corr 0.86-0.996, ratios down to 0.61) although best-lag estimates tracked injected shifts exactly; on the 5 windows with a conclusive counterpart, 7 of 50 faulted copies dropped below 0.998 by <= 0.0008 and became inconclusive
affected_data_or_calculation: Timestamp-shift detection rate of the improved method
proposed_treatment: Any revised gate (e.g. lag-agreement or multi-day evidence) needs a new experiment version and fresh holdout data; do not retune on run1

title: Short faults invisible to both methods
evidence: run1: 15-min flatlines 0/28 for both methods (|PR change| <= 2.7 pp); 30-min daytime gaps 0/26 for both (|PR change| <= 1.2 pp for basic); 60-min gaps basic 8/26, improved 15/26
affected_data_or_calculation: Minimum detectable fault size
proposed_treatment: Report as the sensitivity floor of v1; do not claim detection of sub-30-minute faults
